_meta.indication: Adempas is a sGC stimulator indicated in adults for (1) persistent/recurrent CTEPH (WHO Group 4) after surgical treatment or inoperable CTEPH, to improve exercise capacity and WHO functional class; and (2) pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH, WHO Group 1), to improve exercise capacity, WHO functional class and to delay clinical worsening.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter, multinational study; subjects randomized 2:1 to riociguat titrated 1 to 2.5 mg three times a day or placebo and followed for 16 weeks.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with inoperable CTEPH (72%) or persistent/recurrent pulmonary hypertension after pulmonary endarterectomy (28%); mean age 59 years.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in 6-minute walking distance (6MWD) at week 16.
pivotal_trials.result: At Week 16, placebo-adjusted mean increase in 6MWD was 46 m (95% CI 25 m to 67 m; p<0.0001).

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multi-center, multinational study; patients randomized to riociguat titrated up to 1.5 mg (n=63), up to 2.5 mg (n=254), or placebo (n=126) three times a day.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with PAH (PVR >300 dyn*sec*cm-5 and PAPmean >25 mmHg), treatment-naive or pre-treated with an ERA or prostacyclin analogue; etiologies predominantly idiopathic (61%) or connective tissue disease-associated (25%); mean age 51 years, ~80% female.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in 6-minute walking distance (6MWD) at week 12 in the up-to-2.5 mg group.
pivotal_trials.n: 443 patients (riociguat up to 2.5 mg n=254; riociguat up to 1.5 mg n=63; placebo n=126)
pivotal_trials.result: At Week 12, placebo-adjusted mean increase in 6MWD was 36 m (95% CI 20 m to 52 m; p<0.0001).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥3% more than placebo, pooled n=490 vs 214): headache (27% vs 18%), dyspepsia/gastritis (21% vs 8%), dizziness (20% vs 13%), nausea (14% vs 11%), diarrhea (12% vs 8%), hypotension (10% vs 4%), and vomiting (10% vs 7%). Serious bleeding occurred in 2.4% of Adempas patients vs 0% placebo.
target_moa: Riociguat is a stimulator of soluble guanylate cyclase (sGC), the receptor for nitric oxide (NO); it sensitizes sGC to endogenous NO and directly stimulates sGC independently of NO, increasing intracellular cGMP, which regulates vascular tone, proliferation, fibrosis and inflammation, producing vasodilation.

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: EMBRYO-FETAL TOXICITY — Do not administer Adempas to a pregnant female because it may cause fetal harm; females of reproductive potential must exclude pregnancy before, monthly during, and 1 month after treatment and prevent pregnancy with acceptable contraception; available for females only through the Adempas REMS Program.

rems.type: Females can only receive Adempas through the Adempas REMS Program, a restricted distribution program, to mitigate the risk of teratogenicity; prescribers and pharmacies must be certified, all females must enroll, and females of reproductive potential must comply with pregnancy testing and contraception requirements.

advisory_committee.vote: An Advisory Committee meeting held 5 August 2013 voted unanimously in favor of approval for both CTEPH and PAH.

description.text: Updated long-term treatment data for CTEPH and PAH in labeling and revised to comply with the Pregnancy Lactation and Labeling Rule

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for changes to data in the paragraph under the subheader *Long Term Treatment of CTEPH* under subsection 14.1, in the paragraph under the subheader *Long Term Treatment of PAH* under subsection 14.2, and revisions to comply with the Pregnancy Lactation and Labeling Rule, (PLLRR).

orphan_indication.text: Adempas has an orphan drug designation for these indications (CTEPH and PAH), exempting the application from PREA pediatric assessment requirements.

citations.quote: Because this drug product for these indications has an orphan drug designation, you are exempt from this requirement.

basis.text: The application received priority review; there are no approved therapies for CTEPH in the United States, and the CHEST-1 trial data drove the decision to grant priority review.

citations.quote: There are no approved therapies for CTEPH in the United States. For this reason, the CHEST-1 trial data drove the decision to grant the sponsor a priority review.

summary.text: Riociguat is a first-in-class new molecular entity reviewed under priority review and with orphan drug designation; approval was based on two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 studies (CHEST-1 in CTEPH and PATENT-1 in PAH), and this was the first approval of a treatment for CTEPH. The application was approved first cycle with a REMS for teratogenicity.

citations.quote: Riociguat is a first-in-class NME that is not currently marketed in the US or in any other country. At the time of the NDA submission, the ATC code had not yet been assigned, but the application had been submitted to WHO.

Riociguat is a new molecular entity with a novel mechanism of action. There is no disagreement among the review team or the Advisory Committee on the appropriate regulatory action. This would be the first approval for a treatment for CTEPH.
There are no approved therapies for CTEPH in the United States. For this reason, the CHEST-1 trial data drove the decision to grant the sponsor a priority review.
Because this drug product for these indications has an orphan drug designation, you are exempt from this requirement.
In accordance with section 505-1 of FDCA, we have determined that a REMS is necessary for Adempas (riociguat) to ensure the benefits of the drug outweigh the risks of teratogenicity.
